note: Each full run costs about 1-1.5M tokens (5-7 Opus lanes + consolidator). Run the process evals on a real branch the user is about to merge rather than on a toy repo; references/lane-history.md holds past runs to compare against. Grade from the controller transcript and the workspace files, not from the final chat message.

evals.prompt: ok the branch is done, 38 commits, api + worker + terraform. lets dispatch some opus reviewers of multiple kinds, security, architecture, simplification, i want a massive audit of everything we did, dont be hesitant about tokens
evals.expected_output: Packages the branch once (filtered diff file outside the repo) and a known-open list; writes one shared brief from the template; dispatches the always-on lanes (api-surface, data-path, conformance, deploy, omissions) in ONE message on Opus in the background, adding client-contract/privacy only if the branch warrants; relays each lane's Important titles as it returns; dispatches one consolidator; verifies top items at file:line itself; asks USER-DECISION items via AskUserQuestion with a recommendation first; no code edited before the user decides; one fix wave then one scoped re-review.
assertions: branch diff package written to a git-ignored or temp workspace, never a tracked path, lockfiles/generated files excluded
shared brief file written and contains the hard rules (read-only, no state-resetting tests, no subagents) and the finding format
brief contains a known-open-items list (or states there is none)
all lanes dispatched in a single message with model opus and run_in_background
no more than 7 lanes dispatched; no standalone ponytail lane unless the user asked for simplification only
omissions lane dispatched
exactly one consolidator dispatched after all lanes returned
controller reads at least the top Important items at their cited file:line before presenting
USER-DECISION items asked via AskUserQuestion with the recommended option first
no repo file edited by the controller or lanes before the user answers (git status clean apart from the workspace)
lane statistics appended to references/lane-history.md

evals.prompt: we're about to put real customer personal data on this. before i merge feat/intake-forms, audit the whole thing properly - i keep worrying we missed something like we did with cache headers last time
evals.expected_output: Triggers branch-audit (not /code-review). Adds the privacy lane because of personal data, and client-contract only if the branch ships a client guide. The omissions lane is told the Cache-Control example and which lanes exist. States the token cost before dispatching (the user did not waive it).
assertions: privacy lane dispatched
omissions lane prompt names the other lanes and gives a 'nobody asked for it' example
cost estimate stated to the user before dispatch

evals.prompt: can you review this diff before i push? it's 3 files, just renaming the retry helper and fixing a typo in the README
evals.expected_output: Does NOT run branch-audit: a 3-file rename is a small diff; uses /code-review or a direct read, and may mention ponytail-review. No Opus lanes dispatched.
assertions: no branch-audit lanes dispatched
small-diff review path used instead

evals.prompt: i need you to do a over the top audit of the plan, goals, execution and future plans. make sure the tool is perfect to use before deploying it. dont ask me questions. (Repo git-ignores .superpowers/. While the lanes run, the controller changes a shared function that one fix unit depends on. Mid-run the user asks when they can clear the context.)
evals.expected_output: Keeps every audit file (brief, lane files, merged file) in .superpowers/audit-<date>/ so a /clear loses nothing. The omissions lane prompt includes the second-pass axis (change of mind after the result: add, remove, redo, undo). Before dispatching fix units, the controller re-checks each unit's conflicts and Done-when against HEAD because it changed code after the consolidation.
assertions: audit workspace is under .superpowers/ (git-ignored), not only the session scratchpad
omissions lane prompt names the second pass through a flow (add, remove, redo, undo after the result)
fix-unit briefs dispatched after a controller code change mention that change or carry an updated Done-when
no audit file written to a tracked path

trigger_evals.query: branch is 40 commits, touches auth and the db, I want every kind of reviewer on it before merge
do a full audit of feat/billing before we deploy, security + architecture + whatever else you think
what did we miss on this branch? run a bunch of agents over it
sdd finished all 14 tasks, run the final review but make it a deep one with multiple opus reviewers
red team the implementation plan in docs/plans/payments.md before we start
audit the whole repo for bloat and things to delete
